chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Nak Utba al-Nakha'i said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Umm al-Walad (mother of the child), is it permissible for a eunuch of her master to look at her while she is bathing? He said: That is not permissible.

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: Concubine who has borne her master's child

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a eunuch to look at his master's concubine while she is bathing?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific ruling of *awrah* (modesty) for a eunuch (*khasi*) within the domestic hierarchy, ruling that he may not gaze at his master's concubine during her ritual bathing. This establishes that while eunuchs possess a unique legal status regarding marriage and testimony, their gaze is still subject to the same modesty constraints as free men in private settings, reflecting the broader Islamic emphasis on *haya* (shyness/modesty) in household dynamics. The ruling underscores the distinction between the eunuch's physical condition and his social role as a guardian or observer within the master's domain.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba Al Nakhaie who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a mother of the child, is it correct that a eunuch looks at his mistress and she is bathing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 1. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Utbah from al- Nakha’iy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a castrated slave; if he can look at his mistress when she takes a bath. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not lawful.
